textbookText: UNIT 5 — MITOSIS vs MEIOSIS (Mastery Unit)
Why This Unit?
Exams love comparing mitosis and meiosis. This unit pulls everything together with a clear comparison table and a master mnemonic to lock it in.
The Master Comparison Table
Feature Mitosis Meiosis
Cell type Somatic (body) cells Germ cells (make gametes)
Divisions One Two (Meiosis I + II)
Daughter cells 2 identical diploid (2n) 4 different haploid (n)
Chromosome number 2n → 2n (stays same) 2n → n (halved)
Crossing over? No Yes (Prophase I)
Homologous pairing? No Yes (synapsis in Prophase I)
Genetic variation? No — identical Yes — crossing over + independent assortment
Purpose Growth, repair, asexual reproduction Sexual reproduction, gamete formation
Master Mnemonic — 'M = Mitosis, M = Meiosis' (two M's)
MITOSIS = 'MIT = Makes Identical Twins'
One division → two identical diploid daughters
No crossing over, no pairing
Purpose: growth + repair
MEOISIS = 'MEO = Makes Extraordinary Offspring' (different gametes)
Two divisions → four different haploid gametes
Crossing over in Prophase I + independent assortment in Metaphase I
Purpose: sexual reproduction + genetic variation
The Ultimate Memory Hook
Think of mitosis as a PHOTOCOPIER (exact copies). Think of meiosis as a SHUFFLE DECK (new combinations every time). Photocopy = identical = mitosis. Shuffle = varied = meiosis.
Final Quick Test (Mastery)
Q1. What is the ploidy of mitosis daughter cells? → Diploid (2n).
Q2. What is the ploidy of meiosis daughter cells? → Haploid (n).
Q3. Which division has crossing over? → Meiosis only (Prophase I).
Q4. How many cells does mitosis produce? → 2. Meiosis? → 4.
Q5. If a human cell has 46 chromosomes, how many in a gamete after meiosis? → 23.
Q6. In which stage of meiosis do homologous pairs line up? → Metaphase I.
Q7. What is synapsis? → Pairing of homologous chromosomes in Prophase I.
Q8. Why is amitosis not used in human body cells? → Too error-prone; mitosis corrects alignment errors.
